title: October 1, 1966: India decided tourism was worth its own government company.
caption:
October 1, 1966: India decided tourism was worth its own government company.

ITDC was formed by merging several public-sector tourism bodies into one organization, unifying tourism planning, infrastructure and policy under a single central government company - an early, deliberate bet that tourism was worth professionalizing, not leaving to chance.

ITDC went on to operate the Ashok Group of Hotels, India's flagship government hospitality brand, along with duty-free retail, transport services and convention infrastructure including Pragati Maidan - the venue behind decades of India's biggest trade fairs and exhibitions.

A Viksit Bharat by 2047 needs tourism to be a real economic engine, not an afterthought. ITDC's 1966 founding is the quiet administrative decision that gave India's tourism industry its first real institutional backbone.
